history.description: Kenner emerged as a small rural settlement and shipping point along the railroad line southwest of Flora, Illinois, serving the surrounding farming population in Clay County.
Throughout the early 20th century, Kenner functioned as a local agricultural community, facilitating the movement of crops and goods from neighboring farms via the railway.
Kenner remains a quiet, unincorporated community in Clay County. It continues to exist today as a small, rural residential enclave situated along the rail corridor southwest of the city of Flora.
